questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Explore a new culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit stressful to sort out all the documents needed, including the medical check. Try not to stress too much about it, as everything will be sorted out closer to the departure date or can also be handled in Taiwan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were paired with a local student who could help answer some of the initial questions upon arriving. However, most information can be found on the NTU website or in the documents you receive from NTU.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was okay. There was a campus tour and some other activities which was nice, but depending on which department you are connected to, there is also some specific orientation. However, the one at Public Health was nonexistent :(

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to find something affordable, but I found something through Borderless Houses, which I would recommend.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive, but definitely worth it if you want to have your own room/space.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only applied for a single room and didn’t get housing, so I don’t know.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is quite straightforward. There are two rounds of course registration, and since you might not get some of the courses, it’s best to apply for many.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can ask the local student that you are paired with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend signing up for one of the Explore Taiwan courses, as they are quite easy. I also really enjoyed attending ICL, where you teach local kids about your culture.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some really nice courses and professors (Advocacy and Communication in Health, Social and Behavioral Foundations of Health and Healthcare, ICL, and the Explore Taiwan course), but I also had some less interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three master's courses, one bachelor's course, ICL, and the Explore Taiwan course, so six courses in total.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the courses I took were discussion-based, and you had to be prepared for class. They also have a lot of assignments every week. That being said, the level is not that difficult, so aside from turning in assignments and participating in class, you don’t have to put in too much effort to get good grades.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advocacy and Communication in Health (MA), International Environment and Occupational Health (MA - I will not recommend), Social and Behavioral Foundations of Health and Healthcare (MA), Essentials of Global Health (BA), ICL, and the Explore Taiwan course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Advocacy and Communication in Health and Social and Behavioral Foundations of Health and Healthcare, mostly because of the very cool professors. ICL and the Explore Taiwan course, because it was interesting to learn about Taiwanese culture and visit a local school.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks (boba) are very cheap, but accommodation is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of student clubs are available, and I recommend joining one if you have the time. I enjoyed the outdoor swimming pool and tennis courts a lot.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Exploring the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking!! And weekend trips. If you like hiking and want to hike some of the higher mountains (Yushan and so on), be 3-4 months in advance when you apply for the permits—then you are guaranteed a spot. Unfortunately, my application was rejected. But there are still so many other beautiful mountains and nature spots (Hehuan, Teapot Mountain, Yangmingshan, Yuanzui, Alishan, Green Island, etc.).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's easy; Taiwan is a very developed and organized country - much more than Denmark in some aspects.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: ICL, join an activity, and attend all the school activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Burping and farting in public.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of the local people and the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be openminded, take advantage of the good public transportation exploring Taiwan (and not only the other Asian countries) and don't stress too much about uni work.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoyy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making a bond with the local children through the ICL course.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Loneliness at times and missing my bf/friends at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
